purpose: Execute the planned Mendes catalogue pass against the 1902 Nesbanebdjedet burial, reconstruct the documented gold/body-part inventory, identify provenance breaks, triage dispersed museum objects, and determine the next non-destructive archival/imaging gate.
method_rule: Catalog/archive/museum/conservation research only. No excavation, acquisition, removal, market pursuit, or handling of antiquities. A funerary phallus-related object is a control unless independent Osirian relic identity is established.

primary_breakthrough.source: J. E. Quibell, Note on a Tomb Found at Tell er Roba, Annales du Service des Antiquités de l'Égypte 3 (1902), pp. 245-249
primary_breakthrough.finding: Quibell's primary excavation report states that gold foil in the Nesbanebdjedet burial was used to make rough protective sheaths for the fingers, toes, and phallus of the deceased.
primary_breakthrough.why_it_matters: It directly establishes a gold phallus-related funerary object class at Mendes inside the exact 1902 assemblage already prioritized by the project.
primary_breakthrough.why_it_is_not_the_relic: The report describes funerary gold equipment applied to the human priest Nesbanebdjedet. It does not identify a surviving anatomical organ, a relic of Osiris, or a separate hidden divine object.

quibell_1902_assemblage_ledger.burial: Nesbanebdjedet / Nes-baneb-Djedet, priestly burial at Tell er-Roba (Mendes), excavated/recovered in 1902
documented_elements: more than 350/approximately 360 faience shabtis plus fragments
amulets placed above the inner burial slab
gold-leaf funerary trappings on/around the body below the slab
sheet-gold representation of Isis with wings
sheet-gold necklace/girdle/bracelet/anklet-like elements and stamped funerary signs
gold beads associated with a bead network
small gold pendant/figure elements including Isis/Horus and feline imagery
quibell_1902_assemblage_ledger.interpretation: The assemblage is a funerary body-protection/reconstruction kit with multiple body-part-specific gold elements. The phallus sheath is an especially strong analogue for the project's representation-agnostic body-part search, but remains human funerary equipment.

sequence: local workmen removed hundreds of shabtis and probably other objects before inspector Aly Habib secured the find
part of the removed material was recovered
Quibell explicitly notes that some expected gold elements had likely already been taken
an official annual-report summary states that some Mendes gold objects were stolen before Habib rescued the find for the Museum
museum-held assemblage therefore represents only a surviving subset of the original discovery context
provenance_fracture.research_consequence: Treat the 1902 assemblage as an incomplete provenance graph. Trace missing/stolen gold only through historical excavation records, inventories, museum accession registers, publications, correspondence, and lawful institutional provenance research.
provenance_fracture.claim_ceiling: The provenance break does not imply that any missing object was the Osiris relic or that the missing gold included a special phallus object beyond the documented funerary sheath.

planned_steps_execution.result: The Met explicitly points to Cairo CG 53465-53469 for related mummy equipment. The numbers fall inside Georges Vernier, Catalogue général du Musée du Caire, Bijoux et orfèvreries, fascicle covering CG 53172-53855 (1927). Public web indexing did not expose the individual five entries, so the exact CG-number-to-object concordance remains unresolved.
planned_steps_execution.next_action: Obtain/inspect the Vernier pages surrounding CG 53465-53469 and Egyptian Museum Cairo object cards/conservation records; map each CG number to Quibell's 1902 gold inventory.

planned_steps_execution.task: Identify every amulet/gold/body-part element in the 1902 burial
planned_steps_execution.result: Quibell's primary report supplies a detailed gold and amulet ledger and explicitly documents a gold-foil phallus sheath, plus finger/toe sheaths and other gold body/funerary elements.
planned_steps_execution.next_action: Concord Quibell's descriptions with Cairo CG 53465-53469, photographs, drawings, current accession numbers, and any surviving conservation descriptions.

planned_steps_execution.task: Reconstruct dispersed sister objects from the Nesbanebdjedet assemblage
official_network: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: multiple Nesbanebdjedet shabtis and the 1902 burial provenance narrative
British Museum EA54532: Nesbanebdjedet shabti; curator note points to comparable Leiden examples and examples in other collections, including two reported at the Frank H. McClung Museum
Bowdoin College Museum of Art 1905.25.2: shabti attributed to the 1902 Mendes burial and carrying Nesbanebdjedet's priestly titles
National Gallery of Victoria D46-1971: Mendes shabti of the same priest/date horizon
Leiden and McClung remain follow-up nodes through the British Museum bibliography/curator note
planned_steps_execution.control: Homonyms must not be merged automatically; match mother name, titles, inscription, dimensions, material, and 1902 excavation provenance.

planned_steps_execution.task: Audit the British Museum Tell el-Ruba 15-object place-index set
planned_steps_execution.result: The indexed set is dominated by ordinary shabtis plus a small number of figures. No sealed/nested/reliquary object or published internal anomaly surfaced in the first-pass place-index audit.
planned_steps_execution.priority_effect: LOWER this particular 15-object place-index set for the hidden-container target while retaining individual records as provenance controls. Keep BM EA54532 separately high as a sister-object network anchor.

planned_steps_execution.task: Search published X-ray/CT/radiography/conservation evidence for Mendes/Nesbanebdjedet material
planned_steps_execution.result: No publicly indexed X-ray/CT study specific to the 1902 gold assemblage was found in the present sweep. BM EA54532 has a documented conservation treatment, but its public page does not disclose an imaging result.
planned_steps_execution.next_action: Prioritize Egyptian Museum Cairo conservation/radiography archives for CG 53465-53469 and institutional conservation files for the dispersed 1902 material. Absence from web search is not evidence that imaging does not exist.

current_candidate_classes.value: Confirms gold + phallus + Mendes + funerary body-part equipment in one securely documented assemblage.
Documented incompleteness makes old inventories and museum correspondence important, but missing-object identity is unknown.
Likely key to mapping surviving gold mummy equipment from the 1902 burial to modern museum records.

new_highest_gate.goal: Determine which Cairo CG number corresponds to which Quibell-described gold object, establish whether the documented phallus sheath survives in a museum collection, and locate any published image/conservation/radiography record.
subtasks: map all five entries to Quibell 1902 descriptions
identify present Egyptian Museum accession/display/storage status if public
search conservation history and non-destructive imaging
trace the documented missing-gold subset only through lawful historical provenance records
keep the human funerary phallus sheath strictly separate from any Osiris-relic claim

current_verdict: MENDES_REMAINS_A1. THE SEARCH HAS ADVANCED FROM A GENERAL GOLD/PHALLUS HYPOTHESIS TO A PRIMARY-SOURCE-DOCUMENTED GOLD PHALLUS SHEATH IN THE EXACT 1902 MENDES ASSEMBLAGE, PLUS A DOCUMENTED PROVENANCE FRACTURE. THIS IS A CONTROL AND ARCHIVAL LEAD, NOT THE OSIRIS RELIC.
